input: An amine absorption unit was operated at pilot scale on gas taken from a cement kiln over an extended trial period. Over 90 days of operation at a rate of 15 t of carbon dioxide per day, the unit successfully captured 86% of the carbon dioxide contained in the treated gas. The steam demand associated with the capture process was 3.3 gigajoules per tonne of carbon dioxide captured, while the solvent loss amounted to 1.4 kg per tonne captured. These results demonstrate that the capture performance was maintained throughout the trial at the stated throughput, meaning that the 86% figure represents a sustained capture rate rather than merely an initial start-up value, with the steam demand and solvent loss figures representing the corresponding averages over the same period. Overall, the trial provides a useful indication of the performance that can be achieved at pilot scale on this particular gas, including the energy and solvent figures on which a scale-up estimate could potentially be based. However, it should be noted that, beyond 90 days, the effect of kiln dust on the solvent remains untested, so the solvent loss figure provides no information about longer-term performance, and a longer trial would ultimately be required in order to settle this important question.
target: Over 90 days at 15 t of carbon dioxide per day, the pilot amine unit on cement-kiln gas captured 86% of the carbon dioxide in the treated gas. Steam demand was 3.3 gigajoules per tonne of carbon dioxide captured, and solvent loss was 1.4 kg per tonne captured. The unit is an amine absorption unit run at pilot scale, and the gas is cement-kiln gas, which carries dust from the kiln into the absorber with the feed. Capture was held across the full trial at the stated throughput, so the 86% is a sustained figure rather than a start-up value, and the steam demand and solvent loss are the corresponding averages over the same period. The trial establishes performance at pilot scale on this gas: capture at the stated rate, with the energy and solvent figures that a scale-up estimate can be built on. The two cost figures hang on the capture figure: steam is consumed in regenerating the solvent that does the capturing, and solvent is lost from the same inventory, so a fall in capture at fixed throughput would move both figures rather than leave them where the trial put them. It also fixes the conditions the figures belong to — this solvent, this gas, and a run of the stated length. Beyond 90 days, the effect of kiln dust on the solvent is untested, and the solvent loss figure carries no information about performance past that point; a longer run is the test that would settle it.
